sanskrit: iyam eva sā yā prathamā vyaucchat sāpsv antaś carati praviṣṭā | vadhūr jigāya navagaj janitrī mahānto asyāṃ mahimāno antaḥ ||
english: She is verily that one who first shone forth; she moves within the waters, having entered therein. The bride has conquered, the newly-come, the mother; great are the powers of greatness abiding within her.

sanskrit: chandaḥpakṣe uṣasā pepiśāne samānīṃ yonim anu saṃ carete | sūryapatnī saṃ carataḥ prajānatī ketumatī ajare bhūriretasā ||
english: The two Dawns, adorned with meter as their wings, course together following the same womb. The wife of Sūrya moves in union with him, perceptive, blazing with light, unwasting, rich in seed.

sanskrit: ṛtasya panthām anu tisra āgus trayo gharmā anu reta āguḥ | prajām ekā jinvaty ūrjam ekā rāṣṭram ekā rakṣati devayūnām ||
english: Three have come along the path of Ṛta; three heats have come following the generative flow. One quickens offspring, one quickens nourishment, one guards the kingdom of those devoted to the gods.

sanskrit: agnīṣṭomam adadhur yā turīyāsīd yajñasya pakṣām ṛṣayaḥ kalpayantaḥ | gāyatrīṃ triṣṭubhaṃ jagatīm anuṣṭubhaṃ bṛhadarkīṃ yajamānāya svar ābharantaḥ ||
english: The Agnīṣṭoma they established as the fourth; the seers, arranging the wings of the sacrifice, bringing the Gāyatrī, Triṣṭubh, Jagatī, Anuṣṭubh, and Bṛhat-arkā — bringing heaven for the sacrificer.

sanskrit: pañca vyuṣṭīr anu pañca dohā gāṃ pañcanāmnīm ṛtavo 'nu pañca | pañca diśaḥ pañcadaśena kl̥ptās tā ekamūrdhnīr abhi lokam ekam ||
english: Five dawnings, following them five milkings, the cow of five names, following her the five seasons; the five directions ordered by the fifteenfold — all these, headed as one, face toward the one world.

sanskrit: ṣaḍ jātā bhūtā prathamaja rtasya ṣaḍ u sāmāni ṣaḍahaṃ vahanti | ṣaḍyogaṃ sīram anu sāmasāma ṣaḍ āhur dyāvāpṛthivī ṣaḍ urvīḥ ||
english: Six born-and-existent firstborns of Ṛta, and six Sāmans bearing the sixfold day; the plow of six yokings follows the Sāman upon Sāman — six, they say, are Heaven-and-Earth, six the broad expanses.

sanskrit: ṣaḍ āhuḥ śītān ṣaḍ u māsa uṣṇān ṛtūn no brūta yatamo 'tiriktaḥ | sapta suparṇāḥ kavayo ni ṣeduḥ sapta chandāṃsy anu sapta dīkṣāḥ ||
english: Six, they say, are the cold months, and six the hot — tell us which among the seasons is the surplus one. Seven fair-winged seers settled down; seven meters follow, and seven consecrations.

sanskrit: sapta homāḥ samidho ha sapta madhūni saptartavo nu sapta | saptājyāni pari bhūtam āyan sapta hotāra ṛtuthā yajanti tāḥ saptagṛdhrā iti śuśravāham ||
english: Seven oblations, and seven kindling-woods indeed, seven honeys, and seven seasons verily; seven ghee-portions have come round to existence — seven hotar-priests sacrifice seasonally. These I have heard called the seven vultures.

sanskrit: aṣṭau dhāmāni prathamaja rtasya- -aṣṭendrartvijo daivyā ye | aṣṭayonir aditir aṣṭaputrā aṣṭamīṃ rātrim abhi havyam eti ||
english: Eight are the stations of the firstborn of Ṛta; eight the divine priests-of-Indra; Aditi of eight wombs, of eight sons — the oblation approaches toward the eighth night.

sanskrit: itthaṃ śreyo manyamānedam āgāṃ yuṣmākaṃ sakhye aham asmi śevā | samānajanmā kratur astu vaḥ śivaḥ sa naḥ sarvāḥ saṃ carati prajānan ||
english: Deeming this the better way, I have come hither; in your friendship I am auspicious. May there be for you an intention propitious, of common birth; knowing all, may it accompany us entirely.

sanskrit: kevalīndrāya duduhe hi gṛṣṭir vaśaṃ pīyūṣaṃ prathamaṃ duhānā | athātarpayac caturaś caturdhā devān manuṣyām̐ asurān utarṣīn ||
english: The young cow milked for Indra alone — a heifer milking her first milk of beestings; then fourfold she satisfied the four: the gods, the humans, the asuras, and the seers.

sanskrit: aṣṭendrasya ṣaḍ yamasya ṛṣīṇāṃ sapta saptadhā | apo manuṣyān oṣadhīs tān u pañcānu secire ||
english: Eight portions are Indra's, six are Yama's, seven sevenfold belong to the seers; the waters, humans, and plants — these five have poured themselves out in sequence for them.

sanskrit: ko nu gauḥ ka ekarṣiḥ kim u sāma kā āśiṣaḥ | yakṣmaṃ pṛthivyām ekavṛd ekartuḥ katamo nu saḥ ||
english: Who then is the cow? Who the sole-seer? What the Sāman? What the blessings? The disease that grows alone upon the earth, alone in season — which one, then, is that?

sanskrit: eko gaur eka ekarṣir ekaṃ sāmaikadhāśiṣaḥ | yakṣmaṃ pṛthivyām ekavṛd ekartur nāti ricyate ||
english: One is the cow, one the sole-seer, one the Sāman and one the direction of blessings; the disease that grows alone upon the earth, alone in season — it exceeds not beyond.

sanskrit: prāṇāya namo yasya sarvam idaṃ vaśe | yo bhūtaḥ sarvasyeśvaro yasmin sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam ||
english: Homage to Prāṇa, in whose power all this universe is held — who, existent, is lord of all, in whom all things are established.

sanskrit: namas te prāṇa krandāya namas te stanayitnave | namas te astu vidyute namas te prāṇa varṣate ||
english: Homage to you, O Prāṇa, as roaring thunder-cry; homage to you as the thunderclap; homage to you be as lightning; homage to you, O Prāṇa, as rain.

sanskrit: yat prāṇa ṛtāv āgate abhikrandaty oṣadhīḥ | pra vīyante garbhaṃ dadhate atho bahvīr vi jāyante ||
english: When, O Prāṇa, upon the arrival of the season you thunder over the plants, they burst forth with vigor, they take on the embryo, and thereupon they bring forth abundantly.

sanskrit: yat prāṇa stanayitnunā- -abhikrandaty oṣadhīḥ | sarvaṃ tadā pra modate yad u kiṃ ca bhūmyām adhi ||
english: When, O Prāṇa, with thunderclap you thunder over the plants, then all that exists upon the earth rejoices at that moment.

sanskrit: yadā prāṇo abhyakrandīd varṣeṇa stanayitnunā | paśavas tat pra modante maho vai no bhaviṣyati ||
english: When Prāṇa thundered over the world with rain and thunderclap, the cattle rejoiced then — 'Great indeed shall this be for us.'

sanskrit: abhivṛṣṭā oṣadhayaḥ prāṇena sam avādiran | āyur vai naḥ prātītarat sarvā naḥ surabhīr akaḥ ||
english: The plants, rained upon abundantly, spoke together with Prāṇa: 'Life force has truly extended out for us; all of us it has made fragrant.'

sanskrit: namas te prāṇa prāṇate namo astv apānate | pratīcīnāya te namaḥ parācīnāya te namaḥ sarvasmai ta idaṃ namaḥ ||
english: Homage to you, O Prāṇa, as you breathe forth; homage be to you as you breathe back. Homage to your westward movement, homage to your eastward movement — this homage here to all of you.

sanskrit: namas te astv āyate namo astu parāyate | namas te prāṇa tiṣṭhata āsīnāyota te namaḥ ||
english: Homage to you coming near, homage be to you departing afar; homage to you, O Prāṇa, standing still, and homage to you seated.

sanskrit: yā te prāṇa priyā tanū yā vā te prāṇa preyasī | atho yad bheṣajaṃ tava tasya no dhehi jīvase ||
english: That form of yours which is dear, O Prāṇa, or that which is yet dearer to you, O Prāṇa — and whatever medicine is yours, bestow that upon us for the sake of living.

sanskrit: prāṇaḥ prajā anu vaste pitā putram iva priyam | prāṇo ha sarvasyeśvaro yac ca prāṇati yac ca na ||
english: Prāṇa clothes his creatures as a father his beloved son; Prāṇa is verily the lord of all — both of what breathes and what breathes not.
